# JobQueueWorker class

The consuming end of a job queue: handles jobs and never pushes them.

Use this in the processes that do the work, paired with a [JobQueuePublisher](/api/job/latest/job.jobqueuepublisher/) constructed with the same [JobQueueOptions.name](/api/job/latest/job.jobqueueoptions.name/)<!-- -->. Run as many as you like — each job goes to one of them, which is how this scales out. It opens a worker-mode connection only, so it cannot enqueue jobs even by accident.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare class JobQueueWorker<T> extends BaseJobQueue<JobQueueWorker<T>, T> implements AnyJobQueueWorker<JobQueueWorker<T>, T> 
```
**Extends:** [BaseJobQueue](/api/job/latest/job.basejobqueue/)<!-- -->&lt;[JobQueueWorker](/api/job/latest/job.jobqueueworker/)<!-- -->&lt;T&gt;, T&gt;

**Implements:** [AnyJobQueueWorker](/api/job/latest/job.anyjobqueueworker/)<!-- -->&lt;[JobQueueWorker](/api/job/latest/job.jobqueueworker/)<!-- -->&lt;T&gt;, T&gt;

## Example


```typescript
import { JobQueueWorker } from '@imqueue/job';

const worker = new JobQueueWorker<Email>({ name: 'Email' });

worker.onPop(async (email: Email) => {
    await send(email);
});

await worker.start();
```
